about:
# KnownPlayers

KnownPlayers is a World of Warcraft **Forever** addon built around the idea that you grow to know other players organically through interaction. With player nameplate filtering enabled, the sea of names fades away. You live in a mostly anonymous world, and the nameplates you see belong to players you’ve interacted with.

Maybe you trade with someone in town, exchange a few whispers, or group up for a dungeon. The next time you cross paths, you recognize their name. As you play, more and more of the people around you become familiar through your own actions. The names you see tell a little of the story of who you’ve met along the way.

**Version:** 0.5.3b7

**Tested target:** WoW Forever, interface `16001` (client-specific; standard retail compatibility is not established).

## Features

- Recognize players through trade, party, raid, guild, whispers, targeting, and inspecting.
- Open searchable category lists from the tracking settings, with player history, individual removal, and clear-list controls.
- See class and race icons and filter by class in player lists.
- Optionally open a tabbed settings window with adjustable height from a minimap button that MinimapButtonButton can collect.
- Open **Player History** from a list row or a saved player's portrait menu to see the last activity for each reason and save a personal note or comma-separated tags. Search notes and tags in **All Players**.
- Favorite players and pin NPCs to protect them from inactivity expiry. Use **Undo** within 30 seconds of an individual removal.
- Use the skull button in player lists or **Add to Avoid** in a player portrait menu. Find the Avoid list under **Player Nameplates**. Its default name color is red.
- Create an in-game restore point or export settings, player history, and saved NPCs through Backup & Restore.
- Set optional, category-specific inactivity expiration (guild membership is exempt).
- Hide unknown player nameplates and choose health bar visibility, name format, and guild name display. With **In combat** selected, health bars fade as you leave combat where the addon can update the nameplate.
- Customize category name colors and priority.
- Discover associated characters for Battle.net friends when the client exposes their active characters and a known character can be matched.

## Install

1. Download the release ZIP from the **Releases** page (once published).
2. Place the `KnownPlayers` folder into your WoW Forever `Interface/AddOns/` directory.
3. Enable the addon and use `/reload` if the game is running.
4. Open **Options → AddOns → KnownPlayers** and use the tabs to configure tracking, nameplates, and player lists.

The GitHub source archive contains repository files as well as the addon folder; install **only** the `KnownPlayers` folder.

## Commands

- `/kp options` — open settings
- `/kp status` — show version and stored record counts
- `/kp list` — display up to 10 saved records
- `/kp players` — open the searchable All Players window
- `/kp scan` — scan current party/raid
- `/kp guildscan` — request a guild roster scan
- `/kp help` — show all commands

## Privacy and saved data

The addon stores character names, realms, identifiers, interaction categories, and timestamps in WoW **SavedVariables** on your computer. It also saves available race, portrait, and class information for known characters and linked Battle.net alts. For linked Battle.net friends, it stores BattleTags and observed character associations locally to support alt recognition across sessions. Unlinked friend observations are session-only. The addon does **not** upload this information.

**Keep history exports and SavedVariables private.** In **Backup & Restore → Export**, choose what to include, click **Prepare to Copy**, then press Ctrl+C and save the text to a file. To preview a backup, click **Paste Backup** on the **Import** tab and press Ctrl+V. **Show Backup Text** reveals the full text when needed.

Exports include settings, player history, and saved NPCs by default. Uncheck a section to leave it out. Player exports include character identities, personal notes, and tags. Battle.net links stay in local restore points, and Blizzard's client-wide settings stay in WoW.

### Read a backup as JSON

To inspect a backup, save the export text to a UTF-8 text file, then run this from the KnownPlayers repository with Node.js:

```sh
node scripts/backup-to-json.mjs backup.txt
```

This creates `backup.json` next to the input. You can pass a different output path as a second argument. On Windows PowerShell, you can also convert the current clipboard without saving a text file first:

```powershell
Get-Clipboard -Raw | node scripts/backup-to-json.mjs - backup.json
```

The converter runs locally and refuses to overwrite an existing file. Keep the original export for restoring in WoW and keep both files private.

## Limitations

- Battle.net alt recognition only works for available friend information; it cannot reveal every character on an account or discover strangers' alts.
- Nameplate compatibility with other UI addons and behavior during combat have not been comprehensively tested.
- Clearing a list saves an automatic restore point. Automatic tracking may subsequently add players again.

## Reporting issues

Open a GitHub Issue with the addon version, client build, reproducible steps, and the error text. Remove character names, BattleTags, and other personal information from logs or screenshots before sharing.

## Contributing

Bug fixes, features, and documentation improvements are welcome. Make focused changes and open a pull request describing what changed and how you tested it.

Run `nix develop` to get Node.js 22, Lua 5.1, and the other development tools, or install them yourself. After cloning, enable the shared commit hook:

```sh
git config --local core.hooksPath .githooks
```

**Update `CHANGELOG.md` before every commit.** Add a short bullet under `[Unreleased]` explaining your change, and stage it with your other files. Leave published release notes unchanged.

Before opening a pull request, run these checks from the development shell:

```sh
node --test scripts/*.test.mjs
node scripts/check-version.mjs
find KnownPlayers -type f -name '*.lua' -exec luac -p {} +
for test in tests/*.lua; do lua "$test" || exit "$?"; done
```

We use `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` versioning: fixes bump patch, backward-compatible features bump minor, and breaking changes bump major. Pre-releases append `b0`, `b1`, and so on (for example, `0.1.14b3`), starting at zero for each target version. Production releases are immutable. Keep version numbers unchanged in pull requests; [Martnat8](https://github.com/Martnat8) handles releases.

Detailed guidance for coding assistants is in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Martnat8/KnownPlayers/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

releases.notes:
# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

## [0.5.2] - 2026-11-26

- Added a small easter egg.

## [0.5.2b10] - 2026-11-26

- Add a session-only title easter egg when rapidly clicking the Avoid list heading.

## [0.5.2b9] - 2026-11-26

- Add an Avoid player list with red nameplates and a skull toggle between Favorite and Remove.
- Use a separate default nameplate palette for NPCs and preserve customized NPC colors during the upgrade.

## [0.5.2b8] - 2026-11-25

- Clarify All Players filters and empty results, align the table headings, separate the row action buttons, and show the full player name and realm on History hover.
- Group All Players search, class, and favorites on one row above the reason filters.
- Clarify retention settings, make NPC Manager and settings maintenance easier to find, and simplify the Appearance sliders and color controls.
- Clarify backup choices, keep drafts visible when Player History cannot save, and improve list feedback, history tooltips, and About scrolling.
- Hide settings scrollbars when the page fits and add more space around the Minimap section.
- Center Appearance when the scrollbar is hidden and tighten the spacing above category colors.
- Route the window close button and Escape through KnownPlayers window navigation.

## [0.5.2b7] - 2026-11-25

- Select settings, player history, and saved NPCs by default when exporting a backup.

## [0.5.2b6] - 2026-11-25

- Hide the clipboard selection highlight when backup text is hidden.

## [0.5.2b5] - 2026-11-25

- Hide backup text by default, prepare exports for Ctrl+C, and show the import preview as soon as a backup is pasted.
- Add a local tool that converts portable backups to readable JSON for inspection.

## [0.5.2b4] - 2026-11-25

- Discard pending Battle.net observations when tracking is disabled and block their promotion after opt-out.
- Preserve omitted tracking choices in settings imports and show explicit tracking changes in the backup preview.
- Let players delete either local restore point and explain that restore points can retain forgotten history.
- Report a completed restore or import even when a follow-up refresh fails.

## [0.5.2b3] - 2026-11-25

- Preserve disputed GUID-less history when tracking or importing a player with a confirmed GUID.

## [0.5.2b2] - 2026-11-24

- Check both player aliases for competing GUIDs before moving history at startup or during backup import.
- Preserve the remote realm when an exact whisper sender key is shared by a different GUID.
- Include player history in automatic checkpoints before settings changes that schedule roster scans.

## [0.5.2b1] - 2026-11-24

- Preserve GUID-less history during startup when multiple players claim the same name and realm.
- Skip ambiguous GUID-less backup rows after checking both saved and incoming identities.
- Keep long notes and extensive history in local backups and checkpoint only the sections changed by each bulk action.
- Resolve already-qualified whisper senders against saved identities before appending a local realm.
- Decline ambiguous Battle.net alt matches when looking up a name without a GUID.
- Retry only unresolved nameplate CVar restores so newer settings stay intact.

## [0.5.2b0] - 2026-11-24

- Check the addon manifest and smoke-test startup in load order in CI.
- Reject backup merges that exceed history limits and keep local restore points and settings resets available for existing oversized histories.
- Scan group, guild, and Battle.net rosters when restoring or resetting settings enables tracking.
- Keep whispers from hyphenated character names in the correct history and skip self-whispers.
- Match imported players against staged history without modifying live data or invalidating its caches during planning.
- Restore a released nameplate's opacity during combat when the game permits it, so the next unit can use the frame.
- Refresh player lists once per opening, share name searches across lists, and centralize window navigation and Escape handling.
- Separate nameplate CVar ownership from rendering and reuse the player category color when drawing custom labels.
- Remove unused legacy player and NPC helpers while preserving older health-bar preferences and saved priorities on upgrade.

## [0.5.1] - 2026-11-23

- Add Backup & Restore with dated restore points, automatic backups before bulk changes, settings-only exports by default, and a preview before merging or replacing imported data.
- Show the QuestieDB connection status beside the NPC database heading and fit the category list and NPC Manager controls in the default settings window.
- Expand the minimap settings window to fit the Appearance tab within the screen and restore its previous height when switching tabs.
- Give distance and opacity labels enough space beside their sliders and shorten the NPC distance label.

## [0.5.1b4] - 2026-11-23

- Isolate the database self-test from saved history and prevent player menu actions from falling back to an unrelated target.
- Scope guild records to their guild, preserve personal details, and reconcile later roster changes during the same session.
- Remove stale Battle.net links after a complete friend-list scan, reject ambiguous name-only matches, and update the identity index incrementally.
- Skip restricted unit comparisons safely and retry restoring WoW name settings after a reset.
- Centralize player category definitions, run Lua behavior tests in CI, and enforce LF for release metadata and scripts.

## [0.5.1b3] - 2026-11-22

- Keep custom nameplate text attached to the active unit when WoW recycles a frame, hide it behind the camera, and match the live nameplate scale and fade.

## [0.5.1b2] - 2026-11-22

- Moved the NPC priority explanation above QuestieDB status while preserving the category table's position.
- Grouped player and NPC appearance controls in matching side-by-side panels and aligned the distance, opacity, and default controls.

## [0.5.1b1] - 2026-11-22

- Added one Nameplate setup panel that explains missing WoW settings and enables friendly player, friendly NPC, and out-of-combat nameplates together. Separate checks cover tracking categories, QuestieDB, and native names outside the filter.

## [0.5.1b0] - 2026-11-22

- Made pets, guardians, and totems follow their owner's nameplate visibility when Known Only is on, and added a friendly minion visibility toggle under Character name.
- Enabled the minimap button by default for new settings.
- Added padding around the color swatches and replaced the priority button text with arrow icons for players and NPCs.
- Reorganized settings into four tabs, combined player tracking and retention in one table, and moved colors, names, health bars, distance, and opacity to Appearance.
- Added a Forever retention option, category-specific defaults for new settings, and a combat-only NPC health bar option.
- Placed player and NPC colors in bordered side-by-side tables, updated default priorities and durations, and closed lists when leaving the settings tab that opened them.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-21
